SITUATION: A lone goblin skulker with a copper dagger is closing on the adventurer from 12 tiles on an open road; the adventurer is healthy with a steel short sword.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Goblin morale and breaking points | Goblins are small and break off when their leader dies or when they take a wound; a single skulker usually flees after the first solid hit.
[C2] Crossing rivers in adventure mode | Fords are safer than swimming; a rope helps on steep banks and armor should be removed before swimming.
[C3] Typical caravan prices | Food, rope and waterskins cost a few dozen coins at a dwarven caravan.
[C4] Brewing dwarven ale | Pig tails and cave wheat are brewed at a still and stored in barrels.

SITUATION: A bronze colossus is walking towards the unarmored adventurer across open ground 10 tiles away; the adventurer carries only a copper dagger.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Bronze colossus | A bronze colossus is a huge animated statue; ordinary weapons barely scratch it and it never flees, so fighting one on open ground is suicide.
[C2] Breaking line of sight | Most hostile creatures lose track of the adventurer when sight is broken behind terrain, and slow creatures give up sooner.
[C3] Tavern songs of the region | Innkeepers pay a few coins for a song or a story about local heroes.
[C4] Mushroom farming | Cave wheat and plump helmets grow on muddied floor tiles underground.

SITUATION: The adventurer is bleeding from a deep leg wound after a trap; no hostiles in sight; bandages and a waterskin are in the pack.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Bandaging wounds | A bandage applied to a bleeding wound stops the bleeding; an undressed wound keeps bleeding.
[C2] Pressure on a bleeding limb | Firm pressure on the wound slows blood loss while the bandage is prepared and while walking.
[C3] Smelting iron ore | Iron ore is smelted with coke or charcoal at a smelter to produce iron bars.
[C4] Goblin language phrases | A few goblin words let the adventurer understand war cries and insults.

SITUATION: The adventurer has not eaten for two days and is getting weak; no food in the pack; the road crosses a temperate forest with a campfire site.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Edible wild plants | In temperate biomes the adventurer can gather edible roots, berries and mushrooms; some mushrooms are poisonous.
[C2] Cooking at a campfire | Raw meat and fish must be cooked at a campfire before eating, and cooking removes some poisons.
[C3] Forging a steel short sword | Steel is made from iron and flux at a smelter and forged at a forge with fuel.
[C4] Dwarven noble succession | Fortress nobles are appointed by the monarch and pass the title to their heirs.

SITUATION: The road to the fortress is blocked by a rockfall and the adventurer must find another way through the hills before night.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Reading terrain for passable routes | Valleys, game trails and dry riverbeds lead through hills faster than climbing, and steep slopes cost stamina.
[C2] Regional road network | The old trade road runs east of the hills and rejoins the fortress road at the river.
[C3] Wrestling techniques | Wrestling lets the adventurer grab and throw a smaller opponent or break a hold.
[C4] Soap making | Soap is made from tallow and lye at a soap maker's shop.

SITUATION: A human hunter is skinning a deer in the clearing; the adventurer is healthy, lost and needs directions to the fortress.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Greetings that make NPCs friendly | A polite greeting and a small gift raise an NPC's disposition, while a hostile greeting starts a fight.
[C2] Asking NPCs for directions | Hunters and travelling merchants answer questions about roads and landmarks they have seen.
[C3] Sharpening a blade | A whetstone sharpens a blade and improves its cutting.
[C4] Cave geology strata | Limestone, chalk and dolomite layers are sedimentary and carry iron ore and gems.

SITUATION: A dwarven merchant caravan is stopped at the roadside; the adventurer has 300 coins and no food left.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Caravan food prices | Dried meat, fish and cheap drink cost a few coins each at a dwarven caravan, and waterskins cost more.
[C2] Bartering etiquette | Merchants improve a deal when the adventurer offers something they want and does not haggle too hard.
[C3] Rumours from merchants | Merchants trade news about closed roads, bandit camps and creature sightings on their route.
[C4] Crossbow maintenance | A crossbow's string is waxed and replaced when it frays, and bolts are stored dry.

SITUATION: It is night in a wolf-filled forest, howls are close, and the exhausted adventurer must decide where to spend the night.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Choosing a camp site | A camp behind a narrow entrance or on high ground is much harder for animals to reach, while open ground invites attacks.
[C2] Sleep and watch rotation | An exhausted adventurer sleeps deeply and can be surprised; a companion on watch wakes them in time.
[C3] Engraving stone | Engravers decorate walls and floors with images of the fortress's history.

SITUATION: Noon on a known, safe trade road; the adventurer is healthy, fed, watered and rested, one day from the fortress, with nothing to decide beyond walking on.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Legendary swords of the age | Named artefacts have their own histories and some are said to cut through bronze.
[C2] Dwarven mining songs | Miners sing while they work; the songs name the mountain and the ancestors.
[C3] Cheese aging | Cheese is aged in a food stockpile and improves in value with time.
[C4] History of a distant fortress | A fortress three regions away was founded two centuries ago and abandoned after a siege.

SITUATION: The adventurer is standing at a friendly caravan with 300 coins, a full waterskin and no wounds; nothing threatens and no decision is pending.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Slaying a dragon | Dragons breathe fire and shrug off ordinary steel; they must be fought with ranged weapons from cover.
[C2] Siege engineering | Catapults and ballistae are built at a siege workshop and need operators.
[C3] Ancient curses of the region | Old curses are recorded in slabs and some are said to follow grave robbers.

SITUATION: The adventurer stands at the mouth of an unknown cave that may lead to the objective; it is dark inside and the tunnels are unmapped.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Light in the dark | Adventure mode needs a light source underground, and torches burn down and can be refilled.
[C2] How caves branch | Caves follow water and ore veins; junctions usually mean one branch descends and one dead-ends.
[C3] Farming seasons above ground | Crops are planted in spring and harvested in autumn on the surface.
[C4] Fishing with a net | A net catches several fish at once in shallow water.

SITUATION: After looting a bandit camp the adventurer is overloaded, moving slowly, with a hostile camp 20 tiles away.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] How weight slows the adventurer | Above the carry limit the adventurer moves slower and tires faster, and speed drops with every extra item.
[C2] What to drop first | Drop bulky low-value items first and keep food, water, weapons and bandages.
[C3] Goblin war cries | Goblin war cries signal an attack and roughly how many are coming.

SITUATION: The adventurer must cross a wide river at a ford before dark; the current looks strong and the pack is heavy.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Armor and swimming | Heavy armor and a heavy pack make swimming dangerous, and removing them before entering deep water is safer.
[C2] Fighting underwater | Weapons swing slowly underwater and grappling works better; most creatures cannot drown the adventurer.
[C3] Rope making | Rope is made from plant fibre at a rope maker's shop.

SITUATION: The adventurer is stuck at the river bank: three validations with the same state hash and the ford move refused three times; the ford is two tiles north and the fallen log crossing is fifty tiles east; night is four hours away.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Unsticking the adventurer | Three unchanged validations force an exploration move; a second failure escalates to a re-plan and the same action three times means switching candidate.
[C2] Regional roads map | The trade road runs north from Cragmouth past the pine slope to Boatmurdered.
[C3] Tavern songs of the north | The mule song of Boatmurdered has seven verses and a long instrumental break.

SITUATION: A stray mule stands 2 tiles away at the river bank under a hunt mission; the adventurer has the iron spear equipped and must finish the kill before the animal bolts up the ramp.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Aiming at lethal parts | A strike to the neck can sever the spine and drop the target at once; a strike to the head can fracture the skull and end the fight immediately.
[C2] Verifying a kill | A kill is confirmed by a death line in the gamelog, the unit leaving the nearby list, the kill counter incrementing, or explicit combat text.
[C3] Soap making | Tallow and lye make soap at the ashery.
[C4] Goblin language | Goblin greetings use short barked syllables.

SITUATION: Walking north with one day of food left; a river goat crosses the road 4 tiles ahead and stops to graze; the next village is two days away; no hostiles in sight.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Prey behaviour when hunted | Wild animals bolt at the first approach; a grazing animal must be engaged from melee range before it notices the hunter.
[C2] Caravan prices | A waterskin costs about forty coins at a dwarven caravan.
[C3] Mushroom farming | Dimple plumps grow in dark soil underground.

SITUATION: Three searches of the dead-end gully turned up nothing; the unexplored side branch is visible 20 tiles east on the map; midday, no hostiles and plenty of daylight.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Exploration yield | An area searched three times without yield rarely improves on a fourth pass; the unexplored branches next to it hold what the dead end did not.
[C2] Mining songs | The deep picks song has nine verses and is sung in shifts.
[C3] Cheese aging | Cheese rounds age in the underground caves for months.

SITUATION: A tame mule stands on the trail and will not move; stepping into its tile has already failed to engage it twice; the mission wants an animal killed and this is the only one in radius; the farmer is nowhere in sight.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] The explicit attack menu | Bump attacks only engage hostile creatures; neutral and tame animals must be engaged through the A_ATTACK menu chain.
[C2] Wrestling | Grappling works without a weapon.
[C3] Rope making | Rope is twisted from pig tail fiber at the farmer's workshop.

SITUATION: Midday on the open trade road, walking north to the fortress; the road is clear, the map is known and nothing has changed since the last turn.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Fortress history | Boatmurdered fell in a siege three hundred years ago.
[C2] Rock strata | The road cuts through limestone and shale.
[C3] Brewing ale | Pig tails and cave wheat brew into dwarven ale at the still.

SITUATION: The adventurer is lost two days from the fortress; a hunter with a pack of traps walks by on the road; nothing is threatening and the daylight is long.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-3, indexed):
[C1] Asking for directions | Ask about the route first and about landmarks after; locals answer better to specific questions.
[C2] Sharpening blades | Oil and a whetstone keep an edge.
[C3] Bartering etiquette | Open with a greeting and never name your price first.

SITUATION: Two kobolds burst from the brush 2 tiles away and the adventurer is already bleeding from the first throw; the road behind is clear and the spear is equipped.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Goblin morale and breaking points | Small humanoids break off when their leader dies or when they take a wound; a lone skulker usually flees after the first solid hit.
[C2] Breaking line of sight | Most hostile creatures lose track of the adventurer when sight is broken behind terrain, and slow creatures give up sooner.
[C3] Smelting | Ore smelts into bars at the smelter with flux and fuel.
[C4] Regional curses | The old roads north are said to be cursed after dark.

SITUATION: The trail climbs a ramp to the upper terrace and the prey seen below may have escaped upward; the map shows two terraces stacked in z and no route between them except the ramp behind us.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] goto is planar | The goto pathing never changes z-levels and never follows a fleeing creature up a ramp; movement across z needs ramps and stairs, one move at a time.
[C2] Regional roads map | The trade road runs north from Cragmouth past the pine slope to Boatmurdered.
[C3] Stone engraving | Engravers carve images into smoothed walls.
[C4] Noble succession | Dwarven titles pass to the eldest child of the holder.

SITUATION: The adventurer is bleeding from a deep cut on the left arm after the fight; the bandage is in the pack and one goblin is still circling 8 tiles away.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Bandaging wounds | A clean bandage over a deep cut stops the bleeding; pressure on the wound slows blood loss until the bandage goes on.
[C2] Pressure on bleeding limbs | Pressing the wound above a limb cut buys time; a tourniquet is a last resort.
[C3] Steel forging | Steel bars forge into weapons at the forge with the right fuel.
[C4] Tavern songs of the north | The mule song of Boatmurdered has seven verses.

SITUATION: The adventurer is very thirsty with no drink left in the pack; the river is visible thirty tiles east and the road continues north away from it.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Finding water | Follow animal tracks and low ground downhill to water; running water is safer to drink than standing pools.
[C2] Water safety | Boiling or a clean source prevents sickness; shallow fords hide deep holes.
[C3] Caravan prices | A waterskin costs about forty coins at a dwarven caravan.
[C4] Mushroom farming | Dimple plumps grow in dark soil underground.

SITUATION: Under a hunt mission a wild boar stands 5 tiles ahead at the tree line; the adventurer has the iron spear and one chance before the boar bolts into the brush.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Prey behaviour when hunted | Wild animals bolt at the first approach; a grazing animal must be engaged from melee range before it notices the hunter.
[C2] Aiming at lethal parts | A strike to the neck can sever the spine and drop the target at once; a strike to the head can fracture the skull and end the fight immediately.
[C3] Goblin language | Goblin greetings use short barked syllables.
[C4] Soap making | Tallow and lye make soap at the ashery.

SITUATION: The adventurer reaches the village store with coins in hand and one day of food left; the merchant is behind the counter and the price list is on the wall.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Food prices | Dried meat and bread cost a few dozen coins at a village store; prices rise when the roads are unsafe.
[C2] Bartering etiquette | Open with a greeting and never name your price first.
[C3] Sharpening blades | Oil and a whetstone keep an edge.
[C4] Rock strata | The road cuts through limestone and shale.

SITUATION: Nightfall is close and the adventurer must camp before the storm reaches the road; the rock overhang is 20 tiles north and the open field is beside the road.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Choosing a camp site | Pick high, dry ground with one entrance and a wall at your back; avoid riverbanks and open fields in storms.
[C2] Sleep and watch | Take turns on watch; a fire keeps animals off but shows where you are.
[C3] Stone engraving | Engravers carve images into smoothed walls.
[C4] Fortress history | Boatmurdered fell in a siege three hundred years ago.

SITUATION: Three searches of the dead-end gully turned up nothing and the light is fading; the map shows a side branch east and the road back west.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Exploration yield | An area searched three times without yield rarely improves on a fourth pass; the unexplored branches next to it hold what the dead end did not.
[C2] Unsticking the adventurer | Three unchanged validations force an exploration move; a second failure escalates to a re-plan and the same action three times means switching candidate.
[C3] Cheese aging | Cheese rounds age in the underground caves for months.
[C4] Mining songs | The deep picks song has nine verses and is sung in shifts.

SITUATION: Walking the open road at midday with the fortress two days ahead; nothing has changed and the next action is forced.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] Dragon slaying | Ancient ballads tell how the first dragons were brought down with rope and fire.
[C2] Siege engineering | Ballistae and siege towers break fortress walls.
[C3] Legendary swords | The sword Firebrand sleeps under the mountain.
[C4] Wrestling | Grappling works without a weapon.

SITUATION: A dwarven trader stops on the road and greets the adventurer; the fortress is two days away and the trader has walked that road this morning.

KNOWLEDGE CANDIDATES (retrieved top-4, indexed):
[C1] NPC greetings | Greet first and state your business in one sentence; hostile tones end the talk.
[C2] Asking for directions | Ask about the route first and about landmarks after; locals answer better to specific questions.
[C3] Soap making | Tallow and lye make soap at the ashery.
[C4] Rock strata | The road cuts through limestone and shale.
